subject: Re: Redwood demo — follow-ups on residency, retention & support access
messages:
From: Sara Li <sara.li@finology.com>
To: Maya Srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-07T16:30:00-05:00
Subject: Follow-up: a couple of privacy/residency questions after today's demo

Hi Maya,

Thanks again for the demo this morning — the latency numbers look promising. A couple of items came up on our side that I want to capture so we can move toward a technical deep dive: 

1) PII scope: we need confirmation on what data Redwood persists server-side by default (full request/response, embeddings, KV cache). Can you confirm defaults and what we can toggle off?

2) Retention: we have a 7-year retention policy for certain transaction metadata; can Redwood configure long-tail retention for logs and audit events, and can retention be set by namespace/account?

3) Data residency: Finology requires EU residency for EU customer data and US residency for US customer data. What's the mechanism for ensuring model inference and logs remain in-region? Any documented guarantees?

4) Support access & break-glass: our security team wants details on how Redwood's support engineers access customer data when troubleshooting (justified access, ephemeral sessions, audit logging, approval flows).

Can you loop in your security/SE folks and share a short follow-up with what you can provide (whitepaper/short answers)? We'd like to lock a 60-min technical session next week focusing on RBAC and the break-glass process.

Thanks,
Sara

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Maya Srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.com>, Sara Li <sara.li@finology.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-11-08T09:12:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: a couple of privacy/residency questions after today's demo

Hi all — quick, pragmatic answers below. Happy to expand on any item during the deep dive.

1) Default persistence (what we store):
- Requests and responses: by default, hosted accounts may be configured to persist request/response payloads for troubleshooting and quality monitoring. Default retention is 30 days for hosted eval logs; Dedicated/Private customers can set this to 0 (no persistence) or any cust-defined retention period.
- Embeddings: stored only when explicitly requested (embedding indexing). Embeddings are treated as customer data and follow the account's retention policy.
- KV cache: runtime KV cache is in-memory; we do not persist KV cache across sessions unless a customer enables a persistent store for their application.

Controls: retention is configurable at the account or namespace level via the Console API. We support retention policies (e.g., 0/30/365/3650 days) and can implement custom legal hold windows on Dedicated/Private installs.

2) Retention by namespace/account:
- Yes — policy objects are scoped to account and/or workspace (namespace). For Redwood Dedicated and Private we can map these to customer-defined S3 buckets and lifecycle rules or use the platform's retention engine. Long-tail (multi-year) retention for audit artifacts is supported for Enterprise contracts.

3) Data residency:
- Hosted: customers can pin inference + logs to region (us-east1, europe-west1, asia-northeast1). We guarantee that pinned requests and associated logs remain within the pinned region; this is enforced by our smart routing layer and audited in our control plane logs.
- Dedicated/Private: full in-region/on-prem deployment available; control plane can be customer-hosted for additional isolation.
- Our SOC2 report and data residency appendix (in the Security Overview) describe the guarantees and controls.

4) Support access & break-glass:
- Standard support: engineers access metadata-only diagnostic traces and aggregated logs; no direct access to full request/response payloads unless explicitly authorized.
- Break-glass: for production incidents that require payload access, we use an approval flow: customer ticket -> designated security approver (customer) OR signed approval via our support portal -> ephemeral, time-boxed access session created via Just-In-Time (JIT) credentials. All actions are recorded, and sessions require multi-party approval for high-sensitivity accounts.
- Audit: every support access event is logged (who, when, reason), stored for the account's retention window, and surfaced in the Console audit log. We can integrate audit exports with customer SIEM (Splunk/Datadog) via webhook or S3 sink.

Encryption & key management: at-rest encryption with customer-managed keys supported on Dedicated and Private. Hosted customers can use Redwood-managed KMS or integrate with external KMS for additional control.

Open points we should confirm in the call:
- Whether Finology needs customer-managed KMS for inference logs.
- Precise retention windows per artifact type (inference logs vs. audit events).
- List of Finology approvers for break-glass (POC names/emails).

I'll bring a show-and-tell of the Console audit flows and a mock break-glass run during the deep dive.

— Markus

Sara — quick note from SE side:

- For demo/stretching tests we can prepare a config that zeros out persistence and routes inference to eu-west1 only. That will let you validate latency and behavior without storing payloads.
- For RBAC we recommend the following minimal roles: Admin (full), Ops (can view logs, not payloads), Support (JIT access via break-glass only), Audit (read-only audit logs). We use IAM role bindings per-namespace and can provide Terraform snippets to reproduce.

If you confirm Tue 11/10 09 ET works, I can reserve a slot and bring a prepared environment and Terraform examples.

— Rishi

Thanks, everyone — this is very helpful and addresses most of our immediate concerns.

Short answers from our side so you can prepare:
- Residency requirement: EU data must stay in EU; US data in US. Yes to per-namespace pinning.
- Retention: we want default inference logs to be 90 days, with a legal-hold capability for specific namespaces up to 7 years.
- Support approvers: I'll send a separate email with the names and emails for Finology approvers (security lead + ops manager).

Tue 2026-11-10 09:00–10:00 ET works for the deep dive. Can you please:
- Share the Terraform role snippets and a short runbook for the break-glass flow before the call?
- Add a Drive link for any pre-read materials (we saw the SOC2 summary already).

Appreciate the quick turnaround. Looking forward to the demo of the Console audit flow.

Best,
